newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil loses ground with futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil loses ground with futures.

text.p: NWE gas oil lost ground on Thursday as sharply lower IPE futures pulled outright prices down. Barge premiums were narrowly stronger, but cargo premiums were unchanged.
March IPE gas oil closed $2.50 lower at $173.50 pulled down by weaker crude and a seasonal slide in U.S. heating prices.
Although activity was muted, prompt barge premiums rose by $1 with second half February assessed at March IPE +$1.50 on the bid and up to $2.50 on the offer.
Traders said the modest boost in premiums reflected some short covering in a thinly offered market.
"Most sellers are out of the market having balanced their books ahead of IP week so premiums have gained with this small amount of interest," said one trader.
First half March premiums were unchanged around March IPE +$1-1.75.
Cargo premiums were seen as unchanged, with dealers saying a lack of activity made assessements difficult.
"I can't see any reason for premiums to have moved much this week," said one.
FOD was put at March IPE +$2/4 cif NWE for second half Feb with DIN assessed around March IPE +$6.
EN590 was supported by buying interest into France with cargoes pegged around March IPE +$19 cif NWE.
